  • Constructor Details

    • PbcsClientFactory

      public PbcsClientFactory()
      Builds a PBCS client factory with a default HTTP Client. For more control over the client (such as to use a proxy, see PbcsClientFactory(ClientHttpRequestFactory)). By default, the HTTP client that is constructed will use the system settings, such as https.proxyHost and https.proxyPort.

      You can therefore use these settings to globally configure the HTTP client to use a system proxy. Note that if you get PKIX exceptions, it may indicate that your Java certificates file needs to have the certificate of the proxy server installed.

    • PbcsClientFactory

      public PbcsClientFactory(org.springframework.http.client.ClientHttpRequestFactory httpRequestFactory)
      Builds a PBCS client factory using the given HTTP client.

      If's possible, if inadvisable, to construct an HTTP client using this method that will disregard potential certificate validation steps. For example, a custom client could be constructed as follows: 

      

 		HttpHost proxy = new HttpHost("localhost", 8080);

 		RequestConfig requestConfig = RequestConfig.custom()
 				.setProxy(proxy)
 				.build();

 		HttpClient httpClient = HttpClients.custom()
 				.setDefaultRequestConfig(requestConfig)
 				.setSSLContext(new SSLContextBuilder().loadTrustMaterial(null, TrustAllStrategy.INSTANCE).build())
 				.setSSLHostnameVerifier(NoopHostnameVerifier.INSTANCE) // not strictly needed given the above
 				.build();

 		PbcsClient client = new PbcsClientFactory(httpClient).createClient(connection);
      Parameters:
      httpRequestFactory - the request factory to use

    • createDefaultServiceConfiguration

      public PbcsServiceConfigurationImpl createDefaultServiceConfiguration()
      Builds and returns a default service configuration, namely with the following are true: the scheme is https, the port is 443 (default HTTPS port), the API version for Planning is "v3", and the endpoint path for the API is /HyperionPlanning/rest/. These values should almost always be valid, but there may come a point where one of them needs to change, most likely the Planning API version, if/when it gets bumped to v4.

      Users needing advanced control over the configuration of their service configuration will want to instantiate their own, such as using the PbcsServiceConfigurationImpl class or rolling their own.

      Returns:
      a default service configuration
